input: Map out a week-long silent retreat itinerary

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Silent retreats vary enormously — some are purely meditation-based, others blend yoga, breathwork, nature walks, or journaling. Knowing which practices to include shapes every time block in the schedule.
Whether this is a solo personal retreat or a group retreat with a teacher or facilitator changes the structure, accountability mechanisms, and interpersonal rules entirely.

The physical setting — a rented cabin, a formal retreat center, a home — determines what facilities are available, how movement between spaces is planned, and what logistical notes belong in the itinerary.
The user's experience level with silence or meditation directly constrains how intensive the schedule can be — a beginner needs more rest and gentler sessions than a seasoned practitioner.
The tradition or style (Vipassana, Zen, secular mindfulness, Christian contemplative, etc.) determines the specific practices, language, and framing used throughout the itinerary.

Knowing the primary intended outcome — deep rest, a creative reset, spiritual deepening, grief processing — determines how intensively the days are scheduled and what the overall arc of the week looks like.
The desired output format — a printable PDF-style daily schedule, a simple outline, a digital calendar, a narrative guide — determines how the itinerary should be structured and presented.

gold.taskTitle: Plan a week-long silent retreat itinerary
gold.taskDescription: Design a structured, day-by-day itinerary for a seven-day silent retreat, covering daily rhythms, practices, and logistics.

questions.title: Which core practices should fill each day?
questions.description: Determine which activities belong in the retreat — e.g., sitting meditation, yoga, walking meditation, breathwork, journaling, or nature immersion — so every time block reflects the right content.

questions.title: Is this a solo retreat or a guided group retreat?
questions.description: Establish whether the user is planning for themselves alone or for a group with a teacher or facilitator, as this changes the structure, roles, and interpersonal protocols in the itinerary.

questions.title: Where will the retreat physically take place?
questions.description: Identify the setting — home, rented cabin, formal retreat center, or other — to account for available facilities, movement between spaces, and any site-specific schedule considerations.

questions.title: What is your current experience level with silent retreat?
questions.description: Gauge whether the user is a beginner, intermediate, or experienced practitioner to calibrate session intensity, rest periods, and how strict the daily silence protocol should be.

questions.title: Which tradition or style should the retreat follow?
questions.description: Identify the guiding tradition — Vipassana, Zen, secular mindfulness, Christian contemplative, somatic, or eclectic — so the practices, language, and framing are consistent throughout.

questions.title: What is the single most important outcome for this week?
questions.description: Clarify the primary intention — deep rest, spiritual deepening, creative reset, emotional processing, or other — so the overall arc and daily emphasis of the itinerary serve that goal.

questions.title: What format should the final itinerary be delivered in?
questions.description: Determine the desired output — a printable hour-by-hour schedule, a narrative daily guide, a simple outline, or a digital calendar format — so the itinerary is immediately usable.
